copy.blurb:
The model fancies Korea Republic more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against South Africa. +13.1pp is a wide disagreement by the engine's standards; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Public Elo rates Korea Republic 150 points higher than the other side (South Africa 1620, Korea Republic 1770). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: South Africa to win at 23%, the draw at 21%, and Korea Republic to win at 56%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Korea Republic on the win side reads 56%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: South Africa to win at 28%, the draw at 30%, and Korea Republic to win at 42%. The Korea Republic side trades at 42% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +135. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 56%, +13.1pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Korea Republic side that lower bound is 47% — +4.7pp clear of the market's 42%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 36 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Korea Republic a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +13.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Korea Republic look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 56% vs market 42% — a +13.1pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: South Africa v Korea Republic · the model leans Korea Republic
